lessonTitle: Medical value across the product lifecycle

slides.title: Medical Value Shifts at Every Lifecycle Stage
bullets: Medical Affairs' relationship with a medicine spans its entire life
The nature of medical value changes substantially at each stage
The same scientific question needs a different response depending on timing

slides.title: Shaping the Product Before Launch Is Possible
bullets: Contributes to shaping the Target Product Profile
Early KOL engagement uncovers unmet needs
Builds disease-state education independent of any specific product
Begins mapping the evidence landscape and its gaps

slides.title: Peak Intensity for Translation and Education
bullets: Turns dense trial data into something a clinician can use in consultation
New mechanism, dosing and safety profile need rapid, accurate communication
The prescriber base has no prior experience with the product

slides.title: The Center of Gravity Shifts to Real-World Evidence
bullets: Pivotal trials can't answer everything about everyday, varied patients
Registries, RWE studies and investigator-sponsored research become primary
Often directly informed by insights MSLs bring back from the field

slides.title: Sustaining Differentiation as Generics Enter
bullets: Focus shifts to long-term safety and subpopulation data generics can't copy
New formulations or delivery methods become a differentiator
Supports appropriate continuity of care, not pure promotion

slides.title: Reading the Stage Correctly Is a Senior Skill
bullets: Asking for RWE input six weeks after launch is premature
Running pure disease education three years post-launch wastes an opportunity
Adjusting the conversation to the stage marks a mature MSL, not a junior one

takeaway.title: Medical value changes shape across four lifecycle stages, and reading the right stage is a core MSL skill
bullets: Pre-launch builds the evidence landscape and disease education
Launch is peak translation; maturity shifts to real-world evidence
Loss of exclusivity defends differentiation that generics can't replicate
